text.p: Portuguese cash bonds were flat and futures edged up, helped by a slightly firmer tone in the Spanish market, but dealers did not expect any significant gains today.
"Spain is up a bit and seems to be undaunted by losses in the German and Italian markets. This has helped futures rise and kept the cash market steady," said one dealer.
"Although Spain is always an important factor, I can't go on a buying spree because the dollar and other European bonds are weaker," said one fixed-rate debt manager.
He said domestic buying was supporting Spain but this would stop if losses elsewhere in Europe persisted and dragged U.S. bonds lower.
Dealers said that if Spain consolidated at these levels Portugal's yield spread under 10-year Bonos would remain at around 15 basis points.
There was no demand for funds in the Bank of Portugal's variable rate repo. Overnight/tomorrow next rates were steady to slightly easier at 7.10/7.20 percent compared with 7.15/7.20.
The escudo was stuck in a tight range between 102.55 and 102.60 per mark after closing at 102.52/55.
